text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A 10.6 billion shilling building contract awarded to Mugoya Construction by the National Social Security Fund sparks controversy in parliament whose members question how the company was awarded the contract without going through normal tender channels.
- Fifteen opposition members of parliament storm into Nairobi Hospital demanding to see ailing jailed political prisoner Koigi wa Wamwere who is a patient there.

- Info Radar of London denies claims it has concluded a deal with the Kenya government to computerise the country's driving licences and car ownership log books, saying it is far too early to make a statement.

- Officials of the ruling Kenya African National Union (Kanu) party dispute a government statement in parliament which said Kanu owes the state 23.4 million shillings. Kanu says it is the one which is demanding 70 million shillings from the government, not vice versa.
- The government slaps a ban on animal and milk products from Europe and cautions dairy farmers and traders to stop the importation of such products with immediate effect.

- Employees of railway corporation Kenya Railways express concern over the financial status of the body, accusing top management of colluding with politically well-connected freight forwarding firms to fleece the previously stable parastatal.
